llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备的高熵合金的力学性能，完全不涉及生物医学植入物、多孔结构或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context, no porous structure, no stress shielding or osseointegration, and no fatigue testing.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用SLM制备高熵合金以实现高强度与高塑性的结合
summary_zh.method: 通过选择性激光熔化制备AlCrFeNiV高熵合金，控制工艺参数获得层级异质微观结构
summary_zh.result: 成功获得了兼具高强度和良好塑性的高熵合金
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸测试和微观结构表征验证力学性能

summary_en.motivation: To achieve a combination of high strength and ductility in a high-entropy alloy via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: AlCrFeNiV high-entropy alloy samples were fabricated by selective laser melting with controlled parameters to obtain a hierarchically heterogeneous microstructure.
summary_en.result: The alloy exhibited both high strength and good ductility, attributed to the hierarchical heterogeneous microstructure.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were validated by tensile testing, and microstructural features were characterized by electron microscopy.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of building direction on fatigue crack propagation behavior in selective laser melted Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Fatigue crack propagation tests were conducted on specimens fabricated with different build orientations.
summary_en.result: Building direction significantly influences crack growth rate and threshold values.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation was performed through mechanical fatigue testing.

papers.title: 3D Printing of Metallic Microstructured Mould Using Selective Laser Melting for Injection Moulding of Plastic Microfluidic Devices
papers.abstract: A new method, a 3D printing technique, in particular, selective laser melting (SLM), has been used to fabricate moulds for the injection moulding of thermoplastic microfluidic chips that are suitable for prototyping and early stage scale-up. The micro metallic patterns are printed on to a pre-finished substrate to form a microstructured mould. The dimensional accuracy, surface morphology, bonding strength between the printed patterns and substrate, as well as the microstructure of micro features were all characterized. A microfluidic mould was successfully printed and used directly for injection moulding of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) microfluidic chips, which were used subsequently to successfully monitor nitrite concentrations in environmental water. The characterization indicated that this new process can be used for fast fabrication of mould tools for injection moulding/hot embossing microfluidic devices. It is faster, more flexible and less expensive than conventional micro-machining processes, although the accuracy and finish are still needed to improve though process optimization and hybrid SLM and machining processes.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a fast and flexible method for fabricating microstructured molds for injection molding of plastic microfluidic devices using selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to print metallic microstructures onto a pre-finished substrate to form a mold, which was then used for injection molding of cyclic olefin copolymer chips.

summary_en.validation: The mold was characterized in terms of dimensional accuracy, surface morphology, bonding strength, and microstructure, confirming its suitability for injection molding.

papers.title: Influence of the annealing and defects on the VHCF behavior of an SLM AlSi10Mg alloy
papers.abstract: Abstract In the paper, the influence of the annealing temperature on the Very High Cycle Fatigue (VHCF) of AlSi10Mg specimens produced through selective laser melting (SLM) is experimentally assessed. VHCF tests at 20 kHz are carried out on Gaussian specimens subjected to a heat treatment suggested by the system supplier (heating for 2 hours to 320°C and air cooling) and to a heat treatment proposed by the authors (heating for 2 hours to 244°C and air cooling). The defects originating failure and the conditional P‐S‐N curves are compared. Experimental results show that an annealing temperature of 320 ° C induces the spheroidization of the Si network, which enhances the ductility but has a negative effect on the VHCF response. On the contrary, by reducing the heating temperature to 244 ° C , the original as‐built microstructure is not altered and the minimization of the residual stresses permits to enhance the VHCF response.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究退火温度对SLM AlSi10Mg合金超长寿命疲劳行为的影响。
summary_zh.method: 对两种退火温度处理的试样进行20kHz超声疲劳测试，分析缺陷和P-S-N曲线。
summary_zh.result: 320°C退火降低疲劳性能，244°C退火保留组织并提高疲劳寿命。
summary_zh.validation: 通过超声疲劳实验和微观组织表征验证。

summary_en.motivation: To assess the influence of annealing temperature on the very high cycle fatigue (VHCF) behavior of SLM AlSi10Mg alloy.
summary_en.method: VHCF tests at 20 kHz were conducted on Gaussian specimens with two different heat treatments (320°C and 244°C) and defect-driven failure was analyzed.
summary_en.result: Annealing at 320°C spheroidized the Si network, reducing VHCF life, while 244°C annealing preserved the as-built microstructure and improved fatigue response.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue tests and microstructural observations validated the findings.

papers.title: Bioactive Glass and Silicate-Based Ceramic Coatings on Metallic Implants: Open Challenge or Outdated Topic?
papers.abstract: The overall success and long-term life of the medical implants are decisively based on the convenient osseointegration at the hosting tissue-implant interface. Therefore, various surface modifications and different coating approaches have been utilized to the implants to enhance the bone formation and speed up the interaction with the surrounding hosting tissues, thereby enabling the successful fixation of implants. In this review, we will briefly present the main metallic implants and discuss their biocompatibility and osseointegration ability depending on their chemical and mechanical properties. In addition, as the main goal of this review, we explore the main properties of bioactive glasses and silica-based ceramics that are used as coating materials for both orthopedic and dental implants. The current review provides an overview of these bioactive coatings, with a particular emphasis on deposition methods, coating adhesion to the substrates and apatite formation ability tested by immersion in Simulated Body Fluid (SBF). In vitro and in vivo performances in terms of biocompatibility, biodegradability and improved osseointegration are examined as well.

summary_en.motivation: To review bioactive glass and silicate ceramic coatings for enhancing osseointegration of metallic orthopedic and dental implants.
summary_en.method: The review summarizes coating deposition methods, adhesion testing, and apatite formation in simulated body fluid (SBF).
summary_en.result: Bioactive coatings show potential for improved biocompatibility and osseointegration, but challenges remain in coating adhesion and degradation control.
summary_en.validation: The review compiles in vitro and in vivo results from literature, but does not present original experimental data.
